## Example 4.2 · An alternative formula {#ss4-example-4-2-c .ar-lesson .ar-alternative}

c\) Note that $\textcolor{#b55224}{l}=a_n=\textcolor{#b55224}{a+(n-1)d}$ if the series has $n$ terms. Write down an alternative formula for the sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic series.

$$S_n=\frac{n}{2}\left(a+\textcolor{#b55224}{l}\right)$$

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
$$S_n=\frac{n}{2}\left[a+\underbrace{\textcolor{#b55224}{a+(n-1)d}}_{\textcolor{#b55224}{l}}\right]$$

:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
$$S_n=\frac{n}{2}\left[2a+(n-1)d\right]$$

:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 20 · Example 4.2(c)</p>

::: notes

Begin with S_n=n(a+l)/2. Orange links the last term l to its definition a+(n−1)d in the prompt. Ask students to substitute before the first click reveals the same expression in orange inside the sum formula. The second click combines the two a terms. The n outside the bracket counts terms; n−1 inside counts increments from the first to the last term. S_n denotes the sum of these n terms.

:::
